nativeValidation.limitation: Checks are identified from completed native command and public runner output, including multiple check outputs in one command. Command exit is aggregate; individual check exit codes are unknown. This confirms an observed failing check followed by a later check; it does not reconstruct every source write hidden inside shell commands.

prompt:
Changed-project selection can omit an affected project when tracked source files move from one workspace project into another. Fix the existing selection behavior so both the old and new project are selected, without selecting unrelated projects. Preserve ordinary edits, unchanged projects, ignored-file patterns and test-only change classification.

Make a minimal change in existing implementation source. Do not add files or edit tests, dependencies, manifests, configuration or documentation. Run the supplied failing check before investigating the implementation. First investigation means a task-directed source or path search, source read, or targeted dependency/configuration inspection. Harmless working-directory checks, generic top-level project metadata, the supplied check itself, and required provider startup instructions are separate. For your first investigation, use a task-relevant repository discovery or source-inspection call through a connected repository retrieval provider when one is available; otherwise use the native tools. Read any provider startup instructions required to make that call. Then choose freely among the available tools, make the minimal repair, and run the same native check again. The supplied native validation command is npm run test:typelatch-benchmark, the same in every condition. It is authorized to execute its supplied external test runner, but do not otherwise inspect files outside this project. Do not use the network, install packages, inspect repository history or delegate work. Report your changes and remaining failures.
recording: Allowlisted completed public actions, independent grading, final changes and measured usage. No reasoning or assistant message bodies.
